newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK PPC AWARDS 179.5 BLN DRACHMAS POWER PROJECT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK PPC AWARDS 179.5 BLN DRACHMAS POWER PROJECT.

text.p: Greece's Public Power Corporation (PPC) awarded a 179.5 billion drachma ($665 million) thermal power station project in the northern region of Florina to a consortium including Technopromexport, EVT GmbH, ABB Kraftwerke and Prometheus Gas.

"Pursuant to law 2299/1995, the PPC ... has awarded through direct selection to a consortium of companies the project of construction on a 'turn-key' basis of a thermal power plant in Melitis-Achlada of Florina." the PPC said in a statement.

Standing at 179.5 billion drachmas -- split between 64.5 billion drachmas and 737.4 million marks -- the cost of the project is absolutely competitive according to Law 2299/1995, and has been arrived at through cost comparisons with similar projects at its Agios Dimitrios and Megalopolis power plants, PPC said.
The project will see construction of a 330 MW thermo-electric plant.
The plant will be delivered in 4.5 years on a 'turn-key' basis. Facilities will offer PPC the option to construct a second power unit should future energy needs require this.
According to plans, the plant will be fitted with modern de-sulfurisation units, electrostatic filters and special boilers that contain nitrogen oxide emmissions.
The project is expected to have a large impact on the local economy of Florina.

The plant will create up to 2,000 jobs, though employment will vary on a seasonal basis. It will also offer residents of Florina the opportunity to meet their household heating needs with high-temperature steam. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
